correctness.rationale: After rescaling representatives, Gauss equality multiplies the nonzero coordinates by cube roots of unity. Modulo a common phase the multiplicity types (4), (3,1), (2,2), (2,1,1) account for 1, 8, 6, 12 patterns. The first is scalar and the second forces the singleton coordinate to vanish, so supplies no mate. For (2,2), the two pair sums of fourth powers each vanish. Each binary equation splits into four distinct linear factors and the resulting line has a distinct mate exactly when both pairs are supported; its two coordinate-supported endpoints also distinguish the partition. For (2,1,1), subtracting the original equation from the transformed one forces the singleton fourth-power ratio to be ω or ω² when they are supported, and otherwise forces both zero. Each allowed pair and ratio gives four distinct planes, whose restrictions are diagonal quartics with all coefficients nonzero, hence smooth irreducible genus-three curves. No such curve lies in two different planes. Off intersections and the excluded coordinate boundaries, each line admits two nontrivial relative phases and each quartic one, giving fibers of size three and two. The nonempty open parts are dense on all 96 components; this verifies the difference between E and its reduced closure. As a separate finite check, with ω=8 in F_73 the point (1:10:3:7) has fourth powers (1,−1,ω,−ω); enumerating its 27 normalized phases gives precisely (1:10:3:7), (1:10:24:56), (1:10:46:10), (1:7:3:10), (1:56:24:10). The complex proof uses the phase classification, not finite field extrapolation, and works away from characteristics two and three. No full special-fiber stratification or scheme multiplicity is claimed.

value.rationale: Fermat is a distinguished symmetry-rich example where the hypotheses behind the very-general Gauss-double curve fail. The classification resolves its natural source-side contact locus in geometric components, isolates the boundary where multiplicity of distinct contacts disappears, and separates generic triple contacts from generic double contacts. These data go substantially beyond the familiar line count and are useful for exact projective-duality comparisons.
